subject.title: subagent sessions don't trigger session-memory hook

question: Should bundled session-memory persist completed subagent sessions via subagent_ended, via a broader session_end/internal session:end lifecycle contract, or remain limited to reset/new command events?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but each repair path changes a different lifecycle surface and could create duplicate memory writes or a one-off hook contract if chosen without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define a canonical lifecycle contract first
options.body: Approve one completion surface for child sessions, then route session-memory through it with transcript, workspace, and exactly-once tests.

options.title: Patch session-memory on subagent_ended
options.body: Implement the narrow requested behavior directly, accepting a bundled hook-specific dependency on the subagent lifecycle plugin event.

options.title: Keep session-memory command-only
options.body: Document that subagent memory persistence belongs to another memory plugin or broader lifecycle architecture instead of expanding this bundled hook.

recommendation.title: Define a canonical lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Approve one completion surface for child sessions, then route session-memory through it with transcript, workspace, and exactly-once tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a hooks/plugin lifecycle contract choice, and this handle has the strongest verified current history on session-memory and hook contracts.
